item.title: Getting Started
item.description:
Installation

Android

Haltian Field for Android is available on the Google Play Store. Search for “Haltian Field” or use the direct link.

Requirements: Android 15 (SDK 35) or later.

iOS

Haltian Field for iOS is available on the Apple App Store. Search for “Haltian Field” or use the direct link.

Requirements: iOS 26 or later.

Logging In

When you open the app, you see the login screen with four fields:

Field Description Example
Host The Haltian IoT server URL eu.haltian.io
Organization Your organization name mycompany
Username Your email address user@company.com
Password Your account password

Fill in all four fields and tap Login. The app validates your credentials and loads your organization’s space hierarchy.

item.title: Search and Discovery
item.description:
Overview

The Search tab is the primary way to find devices in Haltian Field. You can search by text, scan a QR code, or enter a numeric ID.


Android

Text Search

Tap the search field and type any of the following:

Search By Example
Device name Meeting Room Sensor
Customer Label ID LABEL-001
Vendor Serial TSE-12345678
External ID EXT-456
GIAI urn:epc:id:giai:...

The app shows auto-suggestions as you type (after a brief delay). Tap a suggestion or press search to see full results.

item.title: Favorites and Recents
item.description:
Favorites Dashboard

The Favorites tab is your personal dashboard for monitoring key device measurements at a glance.


Android

iOS

What Favorites Show

Each favorite card displays:

  • Measurement name (e.g., “Ambient Temperature”)
  • Device name
  • Latest value with unit
  • Relative timestamp (e.g., “2h ago”)
  • Min/max values from the last 24 hours (shown with ↓ and ↑ arrows)
  • Sparkline chart — a miniature trend line (when 3 or more data points are available)
  • Device thumbnail — if a photo has been uploaded to the device

Favorites are displayed as cards in a grid layout.

item.title: Device Details
item.description:
Overview

Android

iOS

The top bar shows Device Details with a back arrow and a Configure button (visible to Installer, Designer, and Manager roles).

item.title: Measurements
item.description:
Overview

Haltian Field displays real-time and historical sensor measurements for each device. The measurements shown on the Device Details screen depend on the selected device — the app automatically displays all measurement types that the device reports.

Different devices support different measurements. For example, an environmental sensor may show temperature, humidity, and CO₂ readings, while a presence sensor shows occupancy status and movement counts. Device health measurements like battery level and boot count are common across most device types.

item.title: File Attachments
item.description:
Overview

You can attach files — typically photos — to any device. File attachments help document device installations, record site conditions, or provide visual reference for field teams.

Viewing Attachments

The thumbnail image area on the Device Details screen shows the most recent photo. If multiple files are attached, you can browse through them.

Adding a Photo

Capture with Camera

  1. Tap the thumbnail area on the Device Details screen (or the “Tap to add photo” placeholder)
  2. Select Take Photo
  3. The camera opens — frame the device and tap the shutter button
  4. The photo is uploaded automatically

Upload from Gallery

  1. Tap the thumbnail area on the Device Details screen
  2. Select Choose File
  3. Pick an image from your device gallery
  4. The file is uploaded automatically
Note

Camera access requires granting the camera permission when prompted. The app works without camera access, but you cannot capture photos or scan QR codes.

item.title: Notes
item.description:
Overview

Device notes let you record metadata, installation details, observations, or other important information about a device and the space where it is installed. For example, you can document mounting height, orientation, nearby equipment, or maintenance instructions.

Notes are visible to all users in your organization who can access the device. They are also available programmatically via the GraphQL API and included in Parquet data exports, making them useful for reporting and integration workflows.

item.title: Keywords
item.description:
Overview

Keywords are tags you assign to devices to organize and categorize them. They help you group devices by function, location, project, or any custom criteria meaningful to your organization.

With keywords, users in your organization can quickly find sets of devices, identify device groups, and see the nature or other specific metadata of a device at a glance. Keywords are also available via the APIs — for example, in Parquet data exports — enabling filtering and grouping in external analytics tools.

item.title: Configuration
item.description:
Overview

The Configuration screen lets you view and manage the settings of a device. Access it by tapping the Configure button on the Device Details screen.

All users can view the current device configuration. Users with Installer, Designer, or Manager roles can also modify settings and send configuration changes to the device.

Note

The configuration page is different for each device type. The available settings and options vary depending on the device model, so you may see different parameters for different devices.

item.title: AI-Assisted Features
item.description:
Overview

Haltian Field uses AI image analysis to help you document devices faster. When you take a photo of a device or its installation site, the app can automatically generate an observation note or suggest relevant keywords — saving time during field visits.

AI features are available from the Device Details screen via dedicated action buttons.

Requirements

Requirement Details
Roles Installer, Designer, Manager
Prerequisite A photo attached to the device
Data residency EU (processing by Mistral AI, Paris)

AI-Generated Notes

The app can analyze a device photo and produce a brief observation note describing what it sees — such as the device mounting position, surrounding environment, or visible labels.

item.title: Map and Location
item.description:
Map View

The Device Details screen includes an interactive map showing where the device is located. The map appears in the Location section when the device has coordinates.

  • Tap the map preview to expand it to fullscreen
  • Pinch to zoom in and out
  • Swipe to pan around
  • The device location is shown with a pin on the map

You can switch between different map styles (light, dark, and other visual themes) depending on your preference.

item.title: Inventory by Keywords
item.description:
Overview

The Inventory by Keywords view lets you browse your entire device fleet organized by keyword tags. Instead of searching for individual devices, you select a keyword and see all devices with that tag — useful for checking groups of devices during field visits or audits.

Requirements

Roles: Viewer, Installer, Designer, Manager

All roles can browse devices by keyword.

Accessing the Keywords Inventory

From the main navigation, open the By keywords view under the Devices section. You see an alphabetical list of all keywords defined in your organization.

item.title: Device Groups
item.description:
Overview

Device groups let you organize devices into logical collections for bulk monitoring and configuration. Unlike keywords (which categorize devices by metadata), groups are explicit lists of devices you assemble for a specific purpose — such as a maintenance batch, a deployment phase, or a set of devices that share the same configuration.

Requirements

Action Required Role
View groups and members Viewer, Installer, Designer, Manager
Create, edit, delete groups Installer, Designer, Manager
Configure group devices Installer, Designer, Manager

Accessing Device Groups

From the main navigation, tap Device groups under the Devices section. You see a list of all groups with device counts.

item.title: Health Check
item.description:
Overview

The Health Check screen lets you rapidly validate devices in the field by scanning their QR codes. Point the camera at a device label and instantly see whether it’s online, its battery status, and where it’s located — without navigating through menus.

This is ideal for deployment verification, maintenance rounds, or troubleshooting connectivity issues on-site.

Requirements

Requirement Details
Roles Installer, Designer, Manager
Access Setup section in the sidebar navigation
Hardware Camera access required for QR scanning

Using Health Check

  1. Open the Health Check screen from the Setup section in the sidebar
  2. The camera occupies the top half of the screen
  3. Point the camera at a device QR code or barcode
  4. The result panel below shows the device status instantly

You can scan devices continuously — each new QR code replaces the previous result.

item.title: Device Installation
item.description:
Overview

The Device Installation workflow lets you place devices onto specific floors in your space hierarchy. You select a floor, view its floor plan map with zones and already-installed devices, then add new devices by scanning their QR code or searching by name/ID. Each device is positioned on the map using a crosshair targeting system.

Requirements

Requirement Details
Roles Installer, Designer, Manager
Access Setup section → Devices in the sidebar navigation
Prerequisites Floors defined in the space hierarchy; floor plan drawings uploaded (optional but recommended)

Step 1: Select a Floor

When you open Device Installation from the Setup section, you see a list of all floors in your organization.

item.title: Troubleshooting
item.description:
Login Issues

Cannot reach server

Symptoms: “Network error: Cannot reach server” or “Connection timeout: Server is not responding” message on login.

Solutions:

  1. Verify the Host URL is correct
  2. Check your internet connection (WiFi or mobile data)
  3. Try opening the Host URL in a web browser to confirm the server is reachable
  4. If using a corporate network, check if a VPN is required
  5. If the server is not responding, try again later or contact your administrator

Invalid credentials

Symptoms: “Login failed: Invalid credentials or server error” message.
